Independent exact rational Laplacian cofactor reproduction
correctness.rationale: Grounding creates two independent arms. The unit injection at position j sends unit current through exactly the first j edges of that arm, giving the common-prefix resistance Green entry at position i. In the unit case the squared Frobenius norm counts 2L−2s+1 pairs with minimum s; summation gives F(L) and F(k)−F(k−1)=g(k). One exceptional resistance x adds x−1 on the downstream p-by-p block. Its ordinary entry sum there is p²(d−1)+C(p), since for min(i,j) on a unit p-by-p block the sum equals the sum of ℓ² for ℓ=1,…,p. Expansion proves the claimed formula. For h≤p=n−h and k<h, g(n−k)−g(k)≥g(p+1)−g(p)>2p², so the maximum possible adverse correction at x>0 cannot cancel the strict descent. At k=h the exact cross-edge difference factors as −(p−h)x[(p+h)x+(2(h²+hp+p²)−3(h+p)+1)/3]. The constant in the bracket is positive by expanding in h−1 and p−1; this excludes the shorter side or gives the exact middle tie when p=h. On the larger side the differences are 2h²(x−t_k), strictly increasing in k. Nonpositive incoming and nonnegative outgoing differences characterize all minima, with at most one adjacent tie at a positive threshold; reflection treats the opposite orientation. The proof includes endpoint leaders and x=1. The supplied stochastic normalization follows mode by mode: for eigenvalue λ, stationary cross-covariance is zero, velocity variance is 1/(2βλ), and position variance is 1/(2αβλ²). Independent exact replay for n=3…12, every h, six positive rational samples and each positive threshold in both orientations gave 4,220 objective equalities and 470 argmin checks (140 ties). For x=N/D, it built the integral tridiagonal N·L_FF with edge weights N except D at the defect, then used leading/trailing principal determinant recurrences and the product of intervening off-diagonals to compute inverse entries by cofactors. All argmins came from this exact inversion, not from the proposed formula. At n=12,h=4 the extra tie x=89/16 gave {5,6}.
residual_risks: The independent finite replay corroborates the algebra and tie handling but does not certify the infinite parameter range by itself. The x=0 limit is not in the claim.

evidence: Patterson–McGlohon–Dyagilev treat arbitrary weighted paths but use half the inverse trace. Mackin–Patterson give half the inverse-square trace up to gains but for Q_S=L+D_κD_S, with finite diagonal pinning. The exact perfect-leader multi-leader result assumes unweighted paths and k≥2.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The weighted first-order theorems apply to the wrong functional. A hard-pin limit of a soft-pin formula can justify which objective to use; it does not supply the exact optimizer changes or prove strict shorter-side exclusion. The unweighted exact theorem agrees on the baseline arm calculation only.

value.rationale: The squared-inverse trace is the total follower variance up to a positive scale in an ideal second-order consensus model. For the natural one-resistance perturbation, this gives a sharp comparison over all path sizes and positions instead of a numerical leader search: the shorter side never minimizes, and the theorem resolves every transition, equal-side case and tie as resistance varies. The value is the classification and monotonicity, not the elementary Green matrix alone.
residual_risks: The classification is confined to one defect and one ideal pin and does not imply analogous migration for several defects or finite-gain leaders.
